In fact, WW, like most CCG companies does not randomize their distribution.
The idea is that you're *supposed* to get an even distribution. A box is not
supposed to have duplicate rares, and you will basically get one print sheet
and then some.

I know that this is not really in keeping with the spirit of collectible at
all, but it's always been done this way, AFAIK. I don't like it any more than
you, but most people *love* this system, and are very upset when they get
anything other than a flat distribution. I once suggested to FRPG that their
distribution *should* be randomized, and they simply laughed at me. Makes
sense... I naively thought that such a process was easy to implement and that
it was preferrable. Turns out I was wrong on both counts (sure, it's
preferrable to *me*, but not to most everyone else).

Their suggestion to me, and mine to you is that if you would prefer a random
distribution, get your packs from randomized sources, dig through a booster box
and grab 3 packs from different places in the box... then go to a different
store (or a different box if the same store has more than one opened), and grab
some more packs. Yes, I realize how amazingly inconvenient this is, especially
if you can get a volume discount from one store by buying a full box (although
it's suprising how few places even bother to do this anymore). Basically, I've
resigned myself that a box of cards has a very standardized distribution, and
you're extremely unlikely to get either a very good box (multiples of great
rares), or a very bad box (multiples of Abandoning the Flesh)... basically it
can only happen if somebody royally screwed up.

andrea....@infinito.it (andrea) wrote in message news:<8b06c4c.02090...@posting.google.com>...


yes, that's the way the commons and uncommons are distributed in
boosters. i've started compiling a list of the content of every
booster i buy, and i already have the order in which commons appear in
boosters if anyone is interested (uncommons are almost done as well).
but i wouldn't really blame it on the printer/sorting machines. well
yes, you could, but the situation is not only present in vtes. i've
seen it in a lot of other ccgs. magic is an example... even with all
their dollars WoC/hasbro doesn't have better common print runs. you
can get lists off the net of the order of commons in boosters. yes,
sometimes they vary a bit (as in you don't get the exact same commons
from booster to booster), but the order is always the same. as silly
as it may sound, i actually like it. if you buy a box of booster,
you're assured of getting almost all commons x2, almost every
uncommon, and all different vamps. this makes buying a whole box a
good thing imo, because even if you could be getting dupes of good
cards, you could also be getting multiples of crappy cards if
distribution was completely random.

and as i already stated, this is something that can't really be
avoided it would seem... i know i'd rather have all my boxes have all
commons x2 (and some x1) than having what i call 'regional
distribution' problems as in, certain cards you get a *ton* of, and
others you don't see ever, depending on where your boxes came from
(something i've experienced with other ccgs, and let me tell you it's
not one bit pleasant). i guess it's all a matter of taste. i have to
agree it sort of makes opening your boosters a bit less exciting in a
way (since you can predict what over half your cards will be after
seeing the first), but again, i prefer an even distribution than a
completely random one (probably because it evens out my usual bad luck
;)

my two cents,
zarrak

It could mean any number of things. It could mean that the rares are
randomized (or "jumbled"), it could mean poor design of the rare sheet (are you
actually ruling that out? this seems most likely to me), it could mean the
display was tampered with, it could mean you have a poor memory, or it could
mean that there was a cock-up in the printing (also very likely - there have
been plenty of printing screwups seen already, and when I've seen complaints
about distribution not being sequential in other CCG's, it was due to printer
screwups). It could also mean that something occurred in the middle of your
box - perhaps ink needed to be changed or the blade sharpened or the sheet
removed for any number of reasons. I don't know the exact mechanics of the
process by which sheets are printed and cut and sorted, but I do know that if a
minor malfunction, or even general maitenance, occurs in the middle of a box's
worth of cards, then it could easily skew the results of a few boxes. So your
"findings" are absolutely circumstantial.

OK, I hate to jump in with what is essentially a 'me too', but I've
just got to vent on this.

My brothers finally got it together and got me my two birthday boxes
of CE boosters. I failed my willpower roll and opened them both in a
frenzy of card sorting when they arrived yesterday. By the sixth or
seventh pack of the second box, though, my frenzy began to diminish as
a chilling theory began to take hold: that somehow I had managed to
get ahold of two identical boxes...

In the end, this did not turn out to be true. Not completely, at
least. Of 36 packs in each box, 28 were common to both boxes. I
didn't verify this down to the individual commons, but I'd open a
pack, scan through the cards starting from the commons side and think,
"Hmmm... this seems familiar," and voila, there would be a rare and
two vampires that I'd already opened together in a pack in the other
box. The first eight packs of the first box and the last eight packs
of the second box were distinct, but otherwise, I got duplicate packs.

Theoretically, of course, I now have lots of duplicates for trading.
